subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool design now, or should cross-gateway session routing wait for a broader federation identity and scope contract?
rationale: The PR crosses Gateway trust, credentials, session ownership, and message-delivery boundaries; automation can identify code defects, but it cannot choose the permanent security/product contract for peer gateways.

options.title: Fix and prove the narrow peer design
options.body: Require `idempotencyKey`, align peer token/auth validation with the gateway explicit-auth rule, add focused tests, and require redacted two-Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Design federation first
options.body: Keep this PR paused while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 defines peer identity, scopes, replay, delivery, and transcript ownership, then rework the implementation to that contract.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Close or supersede this PR if maintainers decide cross-gateway routing should remain a plugin/operator workaround rather than an OpenClaw core surface for now.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove the narrow peer design
recommendation.body: Require `idempotencyKey`, align peer token/auth validation with the gateway explicit-auth rule, add focused tests, and require redacted two-Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The path history and linked issue review point to steipete as the strongest available owner for both session-tool behavior and gateway security/product direction.
